title: Deterministic Policy Evaluator with Explainability and Admin SSO Hooks
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Summary:
Build a deterministic policy evaluation engine that produces explainable decisions (why a request was allowed/denied), exposes a small, language-agnostic decision proto, and plugs into lightweight authorization middleware for API/runtime/Console. Include SSO/SAML admin session hooks for elevated-policy flows and wire a streaming audit sink for every decision.

Goals:
- Deterministic evaluation: identical input + policy snapshot => identical decision and explain output.
- Explainability: structured reasons (rule id, matched clauses, confidence/score, principal/context fingerprints).
- Low-latency path: in-process evaluator for hot routes, with an RPC verifier for cross-service calls.
- Middleware adapters: Go and Node middleware for API gateway, runtime interceptor, and Console route guard.
- Admin SSO hooks: an extensible callback flow that accepts SAML/OIDC admin assertions and maps them to transient high-privilege sessions with audit tags.
- Auditing: streaming audit events (compact, signed) for every decision to the observability pipeline.

Scope constraints:
- Do not change existing RBAC schema; extend with policy metadata and rule IDs.
- Initial rollout covers read/write token operations and Console admin pages.
- Performance target: eval p50 <= 1.5ms in warm in-process mode, p99 <= 8ms.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Deterministic evaluator binary and library with a stable test harness and recorded Golden Inputs/Outputs.
2) Explainability payload defined (JSON + compact proto schema) and included in audit events.
3) Middleware available for API gateway (Go), runtime Rust interceptor (via FFI shim), and Console (Node).
4) SSO admin path implemented: SAML assertion -> admin session mapping -> decision tag propagation.
5) Audit events flow to observability (kafka/topic or cloud stream) and appear in Console audit viewer.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Full policy authoring UI.
- RBAC migration tooling for legacy policies.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Explain payload leaks sensitive policy details. Mitigation: redact sensitive fields by default, allow per-tenant opt-in.
- Risk: Added latency on hot path. Mitigation: provide an in-memory cache keyed by (principal, resource, action, policy-snapshot-id) and an optimized fast-path evaluator.

Links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/rbac-v2/deterministic-evaluator
- Proto definitions: https://drive.redwood.ai/rbac/eval-protos/decision.proto
- Reference PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/4912
implementation_notes:
Architecture decisions:
- Evaluator core in Rust for deterministic behavior and FFI friendliness. Expose C ABI and thin Go/Node wrappers.
- Policy format: JSON + compact rule metadata (rule_id, allow/deny, conditions, priority). Keep current schema compatible.
- Explainability: return ordered list of matchedClause objects with stable rule references and a single top-level decision reason string.
- Cache: TTL-0 keyed cache for recent decisions and a bounded LRU for cold starts. Use consistent hashing for cache keys including policy snapshot id.
- Audit events: protobuf payload with base64 payload and SHA256 signature; include explainability summary.
- SSO hook: pluggable adapter interface. Default adapter validates SAML via existing SSO service and issues a transient admin claim with expiration and audit tag.

Implementation milestones:
- Week 1: Rust evaluator prototype + deterministic test harness.
- Week 2: Explain proto, cache interface, and Go wrapper.
- Week 3: Middleware adapters (Go gateway + Node Console) and SSO adapter API.
- Week 4: Integrations (observability, runtime FFI) and end-to-end tests.
rollout_plan:
Canary rollout in three phases:
1) Internal canary (dev and staging): enable evaluator for agent-service and internal Console for 48h, collect metrics and audit events.
2) Narrow customer beta: gate behind feature flag and enable for 3 low-risk customers with audit-only mode for broader traffic.
3) Gradual ramp: traffic split 5/95 -> 25/75 -> 100/0 across 72h windows, monitor for regressions.

Rollback strategy:
- Flip middleware to previous authorizer by policy-snapshot-id fallback.
- If explain events cause issues, disable explainability payload (audit-only) and continue decision path.
test_plan:
Unit tests: deterministic inputs -> stable outputs, fuzz tests to catch nondeterminism.
Integration tests: end-to-end decision flow (SAML admin flow included) in CI with recorded policy snapshots.
Performance tests: benchmark harness to ensure p50/p99 targets; include cold start scenarios.
Security tests: red-team review of explain payloads, ensure no secrets leaked.
Chaos tests: simulate intermittent audit sink outages and validate decision fallback/backpressure behavior.
